description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of mathematical problem categories across different educational levels—Olympiad-level, High School, and University-level—as used in the MathOdyssey benchmark for evaluating large language models. The chart is divided into 12 distinct slices, each labeled with a mathematical topic, its educational level, its percentage share of the total, and the absolute count in parentheses. The largest segment is “Algebra – Olympiad-level” at 21.19% (82 problems), followed by “Algebra – High School” at 17.83% (69), and “Pre-Calculus – High School” at 14.21% (55). Other notable segments include “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” (9.56%, 37), “Geometry – Olympiad-level” (6.46%, 25), and “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level” (6.46%, 25). University-level topics such as “Calculus and Analysis” (6.20%, 24), “Probability” (5.43%, 21), “Statistics” (4.39%, 17), and “Differential Equations” (3.62%, 14) occupy smaller but significant portions. The smallest segment is “Olympiad-level” (unspecified topic, likely a catch-all or error) at 1.03% (4). The chart uses a distinct color for each category and includes percentage and count labels for clarity, with no slices exploded or emphasized beyond their proportional size. The segments are arranged clockwise without a clear ordering by size or level, suggesting a thematic or categorical rather than hierarchical layout.
